analysis: What changed vs the 8:00 AM brief: the drift lower became a grind lower. SPY fell from $746.93 (-0.99%) at 10:53 AM ET to $744.74 (-1.28%) by 11:54 AM ET, still pinned below $750, and the Nasdaq slipped to -1.74% with the S&P 500 at -1.18% by 11:12 AM ET. Nvidia's early bounce to $163.20 fully unwound to $159.02, and the chip rout spread — AMD down 8.75% at the open, Micron -7.48% — so the AI trade is de-risking broadly, not just Nvidia. The one holdout is Microsoft, essentially flat on the day while every other megacap fell 0.8-2.6%, which says the selling is concentrated in AI-levered names rather than a broad risk-off move; the Dow's -0.64% confirms the rotation is intact. The governance noise got a counterweight: Dan Ives calling the comeback 'ridiculous' pushes against the FT story, but neither he nor Bessent moves the board — the FT report stays single-source and unconfirmed, and the tape is pricing the leadership question on top of the quarter. Macro added a soft note: Empire State cooled to 7.8 with new orders nearly flat, though hiring hit a four-year high and price pressures eased — a mixed read that does not shift a December hike priced near 92%. Signal vs noise: the price action (VIX above 20, 10Y above 5.1%, gold at a one-year low) is the signal; the comeback lobbying and petition signatures are noise until the board or a filing moves. Everything still funnels into Tuesday: Nvidia's print after the close and October retail sales that morning, with Warsh's noon-ET remarks the last scheduled catalyst today.

headlines.headline: SPY slides further into midday: SPY traded at $744.74 at 11:54 AM ET (-1.28% vs Friday's $754.37 close), down from $746.93 at 10:53 AM ET, with the session low of $743.31 holding. The S&P 500 sat -1.18% and the Nasdaq -1.74% as of 11:12 AM ET (Pulsafi); the Dow was -0.64% — the same tech-led, Dow-resilient split as Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Still pinned below $750 into midday, the slide shows buyers aren't stepping in ahead of Tuesday's Nvidia print — the morning's weakness is extending, not reversing.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's early bounce fully unwinds: NVDA traded at $159.02 at 11:54 AM ET (-2.35% vs Friday's $162.85 close), after spiking to $163.20 early and fading back; the session low is $158.11. Morningstar notes it is on track for its lowest close since July 2025. Finnhub has NVDA down 14.8% over the last 5 sessions.
headlines.why_it_matters: The failed bounce says the premarket stabilization was short-covering, not conviction — the stock is still being held for Tuesday's numbers, with the governance overhang priced on top of them.

headlines.headline: Ives calls the Huang comeback talk 'ridiculous': Dan Ives said any discussion of Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia CEO is 'ridiculous' and that Huang is 'gone for good', floating Tim Cook, Arm's Rene Haas, Nikesh Arora and Thomas Kurian as fits for the permanent job. The FT comeback report itself stays single-source and unconfirmed — Nvidia has not commented. Bessent on Sunday called for a 'dramatic shake-up' and said Nvidia should examine whether executives knowingly sold chips to Chinese-backed firms in breach of export rules; a 'Bring Jensen Back' petition is near 200,000 signatories, per Reuters.
headlines.why_it_matters: A prominent analyst pushing back on the comeback story undercuts the weekend's main bullish talking point, while Bessent's export-rules remark adds a new regulatory angle — but the comeback itself stays fragile: single-source, unconfirmed, treat as noise until the board or a filing moves.

headlines.headline: Chip rout spreads beyond Nvidia: AMD opened down 8.75% to $534.06, Micron fell 7.48%, SanDisk -6.25% and Broadcom -3.14% as the AI-trade selloff hit semiconductors broadly ahead of Tuesday's Nvidia print.
headlines.why_it_matters: The damage is spreading across the whole chip complex, not just Nvidia — the market is de-risking the AI trade as a group into the week's biggest earnings event.

headlines.headline: Megacap board deepens in the red, Microsoft the lone holdout: at ~11:55 AM ET, GOOGL traded at $288.18 (-2.57%), AMZN $260.08 (-2.47%), TSLA $380.82 (-2.41%), META $628.96 (-1.98%) and AAPL $353.55 (-0.76%), while MSFT was essentially flat at $523.99 (+0.02%). No fresh company headline drove the laggards — broad AI-trade de-risking into Nvidia's print.
headlines.why_it_matters: Microsoft holding flat while every other megacap falls says the selling is concentrated in AI-levered names, not a broad risk-off move — positioning into Tuesday's print, not stock-specific problems.

headlines.headline: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in Vulcan failure: ULA's Vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes after liftoff on Sunday, destroying 40 Amazon Leo (formerly Kuiper) broadband satellites — ULA's first outright failure since 2006 and the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked. Amazon said it still trusts ULA's long-term plans; the next Leo launch is an Ariane 6 flight on Nov 23 carrying 36 satellites.
headlines.why_it_matters: A lost launch batch delays Leo's constellation build-out against Starlink, but it is a small, early-stage line for Amazon — a sentiment drag on top of the broad tech weakness, not a thesis-changer.

headlines.headline: Empire State factory gauge cools sharply: the New York Fed's November Empire State index fell to 7.8 from 25.5 in October, below the ~16.7-17.6 consensus; new orders dropped to 3.0 from 23.2, while hiring jumped to 18.1 — its fastest since June 2022 — and prices paid eased to 45.9 from 59.5. The future-conditions index rose to 28.9.
headlines.why_it_matters: A softer factory read with cooling orders and easing price pressures is the first cooler data point since last week's hot producer prices — but one regional survey won't shift a December hike priced near 92%.

headlines.headline: Gold extends its one-year low as the dollar and hike bets bite: spot gold sat near $3,862 (-0.64%) at 11:12 AM ET, silver down over 3% to a one-year low; WTI crude $86.75 (-2.04%); Bitcoin ~$64,184 (-1.72%). The VIX held at 20.69 and the 10-year yield at 5.13%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A one-year low in gold alongside a strong dollar shows the rate-hike repricing is hitting everything that doesn't pay a yield — the same restrictive-rates pressure weighing on growth multiples.
